M2_splice_guard_removed._note: Drops the once-only guard around the splice, so the grounding rules are re-emitted for EVERY universal rule they shadow. This is defect D2. It has NO product effect: applyInheritanceRuleStep opens with `if (properties[rule.targetPropertyName] !== undefined) continue`, so the duplicate is swallowed and the write is idempotent — the effect harness is expected to stay GREEN, and that is the measurement proving the guard's product-level inertness, not a gap in the axis.

M3_used_marker_removed._note: Removes the used-marker, so the SECOND loop appends every grounding rule a second time. Same idempotence argument as M2 for the product effect; the list is visibly wrong.

_note_M2_M3: M2 and M3 are predicted EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and the emptiness is the THING BEING GUARDED, not a gap. They reproduce the duplicate-entry defect (D2), which has no observable outcome here because `GroundingExecutor.applyInheritanceRuleStep` opens with `if (properties[rule.targetPropertyName] !== undefined) continue` — the second copy of a rule is skipped and the write is idempotent. Measured 2026-09-25: control 0 red, M2 0 red, M3 0 red. ⛔ A NON-empty red set on either of them means that guard is GONE from the executor: the duplicate would then apply twice, and this spec is the only place that would notice. They stay pinned HERE rather than only in the unit spec precisely because the unit harness never runs the executor.
_note_red_re: `red_re` anchors on the `● <suite> › <title>` failure header rather than the bare `[Xn]` key. jest echoes the SOURCE LINE of a neighbouring `it(...)` inside its diff context, so a key-only pattern reports a GREEN axis as red (same class as integration-test-revert-verify §A104).
